references.reason: A TypeScript resource implementation declaration dispatches the same semantic resource relation as its template names.
references.note: Stage 1 boundary witness: includes primary and alias declarations plus canonical, alias, and as-element usages; ordinary TypeScript references remain owned by the TypeScript provider.

references.reason: An authored primary resource-name token dispatches all declarations and template usages of the same resource identity.
references.note: The exact public-name address is a first-class reference origin rather than a TypeScript identifier guess.

references.reason: An authored resource alias is another declaration of the same resource identity and reaches canonical and alias template uses.
references.note: References intentionally follow resource identity; rename remains name-surface-specific.

references.reason: A non-declaration TypeScript usage activates the resource reference context without becoming a synthetic semantic output row.
references.note: Regression witness for separating reference-context activation from rename-eligible rows.

references.reason: Static $au metadata resources resolve from their implementation declaration through the shared resource index.
Define-call resources resolve from their implementation declaration through the shared resource index.
references.note: Covers CustomElement.define metadata without a decorator or static $au field.

references.reason: Without plugin-conventions transform admission, ConventionPanel is not a proven Aurelia resource; references remain on the ordinary TypeScript symbol and do not invent a template relation.
references.note: Negative control for the resource-index dispatch: the semantic-conformance contract explicitly requires convention resources to have transform admission.

references.reason: Custom-attribute implementation declarations reach primary and alias attribute-target usages.
references.note: Exercises registration-identity matching for custom attributes.

references.reason: Template-controller taxonomy resolves through custom-attribute registration identity and reaches both public names.
references.note: Regression witness for the registration-identity versus taxonomy split.

references.reason: Value-converter implementation declarations reach converter-name occurrences for primary and alias names.
references.note: Expression resources spend the same definition identity as template-origin references.

references.reason: Binding-behavior implementation declarations reach behavior-name occurrences for primary and alias names.
references.note: Expression resources spend the same definition identity as template-origin references.
